t.7.78.1: Having heard those words spoken by Lakṣmaṇa, Rāghava, of great splendour and skilled in speech, smiled and replied with these words.
t.7.78.2: It is just as you say, O Lakṣmaṇa, best of men: the slaying of Vṛtra in its entirety, and what the fruit of the horse sacrifice is.
t.7.78.3: It is heard, O gentle one, that long ago Kardama the Prajāpati had a son, the glorious lord of Bāhlī named Ila, who was supremely righteous.
t.7.78.4: That king of great renown, having brought the whole earth under his control, protected his kingdom as if it were his own son, O tiger among men.
t.7.78.5: By the most noble gods, by the Daiteyas and the mighty Asuras, by the Nāgas, Rākṣasas and Gandharvas, and by the exceedingly great-souled Yakṣas.
t.7.78.7: Such indeed was that king of the Bāhlīkas, of great renown, firmly established in dharma and in valour, and supremely noble in understanding.
t.7.78.6: He is constantly worshipped by those afflicted with fear, O gentle one, O Raghunandana, and the three worlds trembled before that great-souled one when he was enraged.
t.7.78.8: In the delightful month of Caitra, that mighty-armed one went hunting in a lovely forest, together with his servants, troops and mounts.
t.7.78.9: In the forest that king slew deer by the hundreds of thousands, yet even after killing them, that great-souled king found no satisfaction.
t.7.78.10: As ten thousand beasts of many kinds were being slain by the great-souled one, he approached that region where Mahāsena had been born.
t.7.78.11: There Hara, lord of the god of gods, delighted the daughter of the king of mountains, together with all his invincible attendants.
t.7.78.12: There, by that mountain waterfall, Umeśa, whose banner bears the bull, wishing to do what was pleasing to the Goddess, made himself into a woman.
t.7.78.13: And whatever creatures in that part of the forest were called male, and whatever else there was besides, all of it came to bear the name of female.
t.7.78.14: Meanwhile that king Ila, the son of Kardama, slaying thousands of deer, approached that region.
t.7.78.15: He saw that everything, with its beasts of prey, deer and birds, had been turned female, and that he himself, together with his followers, had become a woman, O Raghunandana.
t.7.78.16: Great indeed was his sorrow on seeing himself in such a state, and, knowing that this was the deed of Umāpati, he was seized with fear.
t.7.78.17: Then the king, together with his servants, troops and mounts, went for refuge to the great-souled god, the blue-throated one with matted locks.
t.7.78.18: Then the illustrious bestower of boons, together with the Goddess, laughed, and the bestower of boons himself spoke these words to the son of Prajāpati.
t.7.78.19: Rise, rise, O royal sage, mighty son of Kardama! Except for manhood, O gentle one, choose a boon, O you of good vows.
t.7.78.20: Then the king, stricken with grief and refused by the great-souled one, did not accept any other boon from the best of gods, for he had become a woman.
t.7.78.21: Then the king, in great sorrow, bowed down with his whole inner self before the great goddess, the daughter of the king of mountains.
t.7.78.23: Having understood what lay in the heart of that royal sage, the goddess, esteemed by Rudra, replied with auspicious words in the presence of Hara.
t.7.78.22: O sovereign of boons, O bestower of boons, you are the giver of boons to the worlds, O beautiful lady! O goddess whose glance is never in vain, I worship you; O gentle one, salutation be to you.
t.7.78.24: The god is the giver of half of the boon, and I likewise grant the other half; therefore take for yourself a half of woman and man, for as long as you wish.
t.7.78.25: Having heard that most wondrous and unsurpassed boon of the goddess, the king, his mind filled with great joy, then spoke these words.
t.7.78.26: O goddess, unequalled in beauty upon the earth, if you are pleased with me, then, after living as a woman for a month, may I be a man again for a month.
t.7.78.27: Understanding what he desired, the goddess of most lovely countenance replied with auspicious words: "So shall this be."
t.7.78.28: O king, when you have become a man, you will not remember your womanhood; and having become a woman for the following month, you will not remember your manhood.
t.7.78.29: Thus that king, the son of Kardama, having been a man for a month, then became Ilā, a woman most beautiful in the three worlds, for one month.
